summary: The unit test suite (SemanticVersionBumper.Tests.ps1) is excellent—it comprehensively tests all core functions (version parsing, bump logic, changelog generation, commit parsing) with good edge case coverage (empty files, malformed versions, scoped commits, breaking changes). However, the acceptance test suite (Workflow.Acceptance.Tests.ps1) has a critical incompleteness: it references fixture files at `fixtures/feat-minor/`, `fixtures/fix-patch/`, `fixtures/breaking-major/`, and `fixtures/pkgjson-minor/` but does not create them and they are not provided in the workspace. The acceptance tests will fail at the `Copy-Item` step when attempting to stage these fixtures into temp git repos. The unit tests also do not test empty commit logs, pre-release/build-metadata versions, missing initial version files, or GITHUB_OUTPUT integration in the CLI wrapper. The workflow structure validation and act execution framework are well-designed, but the missing fixture definitions make the acceptance tests incomplete. The case matrix is duplicated (discovery vs. runtime scope) to work around Pester limitations, adding maintenance burden. Assuming fixtures existed, this would be a 4/5 suite; as provided, the dependency gap reduces confidence in end-to-end correctness.
